You're given that a robe takes 2 bolts of blue fiber and n bolts of white fiber.  So you're trying to find the total number of bolts that this robe takes (2 + n). The total number of bolts  of fiber used is actually a constant, 3n + 2 (6n). The number of bolts taken for blue and white fiber differ only by a constant. You can then think of this as an algebra question in 2 variables where one of the variables is equal to another expression.  In this case, n will equal 2 + 2.  So you can calculate n to equal 4 (and applying n = 4, the total comes to 14).  Just as a side note, in most countries, clothing isn't made with bolts of fiber, but you can  clip off desired amounts of yardage from them, in yardage units  (and if you clip shorter pieces, you can use our strategy to calculate not just lengths of fabric  that the length of the desired piece of fabric is (4 + a) given that a is the length of that (clipped piece)  you can also calculate the yardage of the fabric which was clipped).
